newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends stable on renewed confidence.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends stable on renewed confidence.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices closed higher on shortcovering of the SMR20 by dealers confident of an intervention from INRO if the market fell further.
Traders said they noted bidding for small consignments of the SMR20 by fellow dealers anticipating support for the grade from the International Natural Rubber Organisation (INRO).
Dealers said INRO was poised to buy up the grade anytime if the five-day average price of rubber dipped to 172 cents.
At the close, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board (MRELB) quoted the benchmark RSS1 buyer for August at 228.50 cents (90 U.S. cents) a kg, up half cent from Friday.
The board, however, quoted the SMR 20 buyer for August at 232.50 cents, unchanged.
Traders quoted the SMR 20 at 234 cents, SMR CV at 295, SMR L at 278, SMR5 at 245, SMR10 at 237 and drum latex at 193.
The INRO's five-day average price was at 182.07 cents a kg on July 11, compared to the 182.48 cents on July 10.
Malaysian-based shipping brokers quoted freight rates for rubber from Malaysia to Rotterdam at $700 per 20-ft container, and $1,400 per 40-ft container.
